items.title: Defensieve problemen bij NEC in aanloop naar Olympiakos
items.summary: NEC neemt het dinsdagavond in de derde voorronde van de Champions League op tegen Olympiakos. Clubwatcher Sander Janssen vertelt in VI Rondje Europa Extra over de personele problemen achterin en alle transferperikelen die spelen. Janssen verwacht bijvoorbeeld dat zowel Kodai Sano (interesse PSV) als Sami Ouaissa (interesse Feyenoord) nog vertrekken bij de Nijmegenaren.

items.title: WK-held Vozinha (40) wordt groots onthaald bij nieuwe club
items.summary: Er leek even een kink in de kabel, maar Vozinha is op grootse wijze onthaald bij zijn nieuwe club Colo-Colo. Vozinha, die uitblonk onder de lat van Kaapverdië op het WK, werd door hordes Chileense fans opgewacht bij zijn aankomst in de hoofdstad Santiago. De routinier stond voor het laatst onder contract bij het Portugese Chaves en verdedigde eerder de doelen van onder meer AS Trencin, AEL Limassol, Gil Vicente en Zimbru Chisinau.

items.title: ‘I can’t wait’: Dominik Szoboszlai hungry for Liverpool reset under Andoni Iraola
items.summary: Midfielder adapting to life under new manager Reds need ‘something special’ without further additions Dominik Szoboszlai believes last season’s frustration can push Liverpool to challenge for the title again but admits the squad must produce “something special” if no reinforcements arrive before the transfer deadline. The Liverpool midfielder upped his already impressive level last season, being named the club’s player of the year, but collectively the team went into reverse with Arne Slot losing his job as a consequence. The poor title defence from a team that won the Premier League comfortably in Slot’s debut season should, Szoboszlai insists, prompt a reaction in Andoni Iraola’s debut campaign as Liverpool head coach. items.title: Football transfer rumours: Chelsea’s Mudryk to reunite with Lampard at Coventry?
items.summary: Today’s rumours broke you once, made you strong Cody Gakpo’s performances went south last season and now his entire personage might follow, with Tottenham Hotspur reportedly preparing an offer in the region of £70m to bring him to north London. There appears to be some mixed messages floating around about this potential deal. The Mail say Liverpool “have no plans to sell Gakpo” and that “it would take a huge sum to change their stance”, but these things are fluid. The Athletic say “Liverpool have no intention of selling”, but also, and in the same sentence, that they “would judge his value relative to other deals this summer, including Morgan Rogers’ transfer to Chelsea”. So, in short, Spurs will have to whip out their recently-discovered XXL chequebook if they want to get this one over the line. Talking about Chelsea, “multiple Premier League clubs” have contacted them to ask about the availability of Mykhailo Mudryk, recently freed from a doping ban, says the Mirror. They name only one of them: Coventry City, coached by two-time former Stamford Bridge manager Frank Lampard. The Sun specify that “two more Prem sides are believed to have enquired, while there is interest from three clubs in Europe”. The Mirror’s report on the battle for the Ukrainian’s services is inevitably, but pleasingly, headlined “Mud Fight”. Continue reading...

items.title: Alverca: the Portuguese club thriving with help from Vinícius Júnior
items.summary: Their rise is down to smart scouting and clever links with celebrities such as Eduardo Camavinga and Travis Scott By Get French Football News Alverca have been busy in the last few years. They have shot up the Portuguese pyramid while changing owners, buying a whole new squad and bringing in one of the world’s most famous footballers as a co-owner. The club’s sporting director, Fernando Malta, says they want to be “gamechangers”. Historically a satellite club for nearby Benfica, Alverca were first promoted to the top flight in 1998 but folded in 2005 after a costly relegation. The club reformed and gradually made its way through the regional divisions before earning back-to-back promotions to take them to the Portuguese top flight in 2025. Continue reading...

items.title: Charlton up for sale again as US owners look to cash in after three years
items.summary: Owners led by Gabriel Brener paid £15m in 2023 Buyer would be the club’s fifth owner in six years Charlton’s US owners have put the club up for sale just three years after taking over at the Valley. The ownership group is understood to have engaged Oakwell Sports Advisory to find what would be the club’s fifth owner in the past six years. In a sales deck sent to potential investors, which has been seen by the Guardian, Oakwell describes Charlton as “the last remaining football club upside opportunity in London”. Oakwell also claims that Charlton would provide new owners with an opportunity for five to 10 times equity growth through promotion to the Premier League, commercial expansion and investment in women’s football.
